doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Winning a raise from Hampton and Joe Glaser
summary: Earning eleven dollars a night with Hampton, Wilder was sent to Gladys Hampton and manager Joe Glaser, told Glaser off, and got fifteen dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. You had a lot of that. And you would go work in clubs and things and they would pay the guys a pittance. They were making good money but they wouldn’t give it to them. Well Lionel Hampton was a good case in point. I joined that band and I was making eleven dollars a night, and I was playing, at that time, the first trumpet part. I wasn’t playing the high things, he had guys there, Ernie Royal and guys who did that. But I was supposed to be the first trumpet player and I was getting eleven dollars a night, and I asked him at one point when I discovered that the other guys, some of them, were getting fifteen, I thought well why can’t I get fifteen too? And I asked him about it and he said, “well you’d better speak to Gladys” his wife. And he said, “she takes care of that.” So I spoke to her and she said, “yes what is it, young man?” And I said, “well I’d like to get fifteen dollars a night like everybody else.” She said, “well honey you better talk to Joe Glaser” who was the manager. And so I called his office and made an appointment to see him. And a couple days hence I went to his office, at the time, two o’clock like he says. And when I walked in his secretary said, “who are you?” And I said, “well my name is Joe Wilder, and Mrs. Hampton told me to come and see Mr. Glaser, and I made an appointment for two o’clock.” And she said okay. She called him on the intercom and he said okay send him in. And when I went in he said, “what do you want?” And I said “well Mrs. Hampton told me to come and speak to you about getting a raise.” He said, © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-

“hey” — if you will excuse the language — “who in the hell do you think you are?” This was exactly the way he asked me. And I looked at him and I said, “who in the hell do you think YOU are?” And I turned around and walked out and that night I told Lionel, I said, “if I don’t get fifteen dollars a night from tonight on, I’m out, you’ll have to get somebody else.” And so he said, “well I’ll talk to Gladys about it.” So he spoke to her and as of the next night they did pay me fifteen dollars a night. But that was the attitude towards the musicians and unfortunately I mean in some places it still prevails.
And probably some other musicians would have not pursued it like you did.
No, well they might have been intimidated by it, not that I wasn’t too, I mean to some extent I was. I mean I’m a young kid. But that’s the way it went.
